paragraphs.title: The War against Jerusalem and the Lord’s Manifestation

easy.explanation: The passage says that all nations will be gathered against Jerusalem to battle.
easy.q: Against which city will all nations be gathered to battle?

answers: It will be covered with water
easy.explanation: The mount of Olives will cleave in the midst from east to west.
easy.q: What will happen to the mount of Olives?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the LORD will go forth and fight against those nations.
easy.q: Who will fight against the nations?

answers: A great valley and a way of escape will be formed
The sea will reach the city
medium.explanation: The divided mountain will form a very great valley through which the people can flee.
medium.q: What will result from the splitting of the mount of Olives?

medium.explanation: The KJV phrase describes the houses being entered and robbed by the invaders.
medium.q: What does “the houses rifled” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD fights, and afterward the nations arrive
The mount of Olives splits before the battle
The nations attack, and then the LORD appears and fights
medium.explanation: The nations first attack Jerusalem; afterward the LORD goes forth to fight them.
medium.q: What is the order of events described in the passage?

answers: Jerusalem is afflicted, but the LORD comes to deliver it
The nations flee before they arrive
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem is taken and harmed, but the LORD appears and fights against its enemies.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in this passage?

answers: All the city’s inhabitants are saved
The city and its people are not completely cut off
There is no battle in the city
challenge.explanation: Half of the city goes into captivity, while the residue of the people remains.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that only part of the city goes into captivity?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says that the mountain will cleave toward the east and toward the west.
challenge.q: In what direction does the mount of Olives split?

paragraphs.title: The New Light and the Living Waters

easy.explanation: The passage says that living waters will go out from Jerusalem.
easy.q: What will go out from Jerusalem?

answers: Toward the former sea and the hinder sea
easy.explanation: Half of the waters will flow toward each of the two seas.
The passage declares that the LORD shall be king over all the earth.
easy.q: Who will be king over all the earth?

answers: It will not follow the ordinary division of day and night
medium.explanation: It will not be an ordinary day or night, and at evening time there will be light.
medium.q: What will be unusual about the day described?

answers: Water flowing from Jerusalem toward two seas
medium.explanation: The verse describes waters going out from Jerusalem and flowing in two directions.
medium.q: What are the “living waters” in this passage?

answers: The waters flow only in winter
The waters are part of the new and continuing order
medium.explanation: The waters will be present in summer and winter, as part of the renewed reality.
medium.q: What is the connection between the living waters and the change in the land?

answers: The LORD’s unique kingship and name
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that there will be one LORD and his name one.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repetition of “one” in the verse?

answers: The waters depend on only one season
The flow is described as continuing throughout the year
The waters will disappear in winter
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the waters will be present in both summer and winter.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the waters flowing in summer and winter?

answers: The land becomes a plain and Jerusalem is lifted up
challenge.explanation: The land will be turned as a plain, while Jerusalem will be lifted up and inhabited in her place.
challenge.q: What geographical change is described concerning Jerusalem and the land?

paragraphs.title: Jerusalem’s Security and the Defeat of Its Enemies

easy.explanation: The passage says that Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.

answers: They will suffer plague and confusion
easy.explanation: The enemies will be struck by plague and a great tumult.
easy.q: What will happen to the enemies?

easy.explanation: The wealth of the nations, including gold, silver, and apparel, will be gathered.
easy.q: What will be gathered from the nations?

medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means that Jerusalem will no longer be completely destroyed.
medium.q: What does “utter destruction” mean in the sentence “there shall be no more utter destruction”?

answers: His hand will rise against his neighbour’s hand
They will flee to the sea
medium.explanation: The passage describes people turning against one another in the confusion.
medium.q: What will happen when each person lays hold on the hand of his neighbour?

answers: The nations fighting against Jerusalem and the animals in their camps
medium.explanation: The plague will strike the enemies and the beasts in their tents.
medium.q: Who will be affected by the plague?

answers: Jerusalem dwells safely, while its enemies suffer defeat
The enemies dwell safely while the city is destroyed
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem is safely inhabited, while the enemies suffer plague and confusion.
challenge.q: What contrast stands out between Jerusalem and its enemies?

answers: The plague is limited to the enemy leaders
The defeat extends to the enemy camps and their animals
challenge.explanation: The passage extends the plague beyond the soldiers to the animals in the camps.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the plague affecting horses, mules, camels, and asses?

answers: Judah will also take part in the battle at Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What does “Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem” mean?

answers: Go up to Jerusalem every year
easy.explanation: The nations that remain will go up from year to year to Jerusalem.
easy.q: What will the nations that remain do?

answers: To worship the LORD and keep the feast of tabernacles
easy.explanation: They will go up to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and keep the feast.
easy.q: Why will the nations go up to Jerusalem?

answers: They will have no rain or will suffer plague
easy.explanation: Those who refuse to go up will face a lack of rain or the plague.
easy.q: What will happen to those who do not go up?

answers: Going up is connected with receiving rain
medium.explanation: Those who do not go up to worship will have no rain.
medium.q: What is the connection between going up to Jerusalem and rain?

medium.explanation: The expression describes an action repeated each year.
medium.q: What does “from year to year” mean?

answers: Plague if it does not go up to keep the feast
medium.explanation: Egypt will be struck with the plague if it does not go up to keep the feast.
medium.q: What special punishment is described for Egypt?

answers: They must go up to Jerusalem and worship the LORD
They must permanently leave their lands
challenge.explanation: All the nations that remain are required to go up and worship the LORD.
challenge.q: What common requirement applies to the nations that remain?

answers: Refusing to keep the feast brings blessing
Refusing to keep the feast brings lack of rain or plague
challenge.explanation: The passage presents lack of rain or plague as the consequence of refusing to go up.

answers: Egypt is not counted as a nation
Egypt is exempt from the feast
Egypt must also participate and will be punished if it refuses
challenge.explanation: Egypt is specifically included among those required to go up and keep the feast.
challenge.q: What is significant about Egypt being included in the requirement?

paragraphs.title: The Holiness of the Temple and the Renewed World

easy.explanation: The bells of the horses will bear the words “HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD.”
easy.q: What will be written upon the bells of the horses?

easy.explanation: The passage says that every pot in Jerusalem and Judah shall be holiness unto the LORD.
easy.q: What will be holy in Jerusalem and Judah?

easy.explanation: The verse says that there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What will no longer be in the house of the LORD?

medium.explanation: The pots in the LORD’s house will be like the bowls before the altar.
medium.q: To what will the pots in the LORD’s house be compared?

medium.explanation: The verse refers to bells worn by the horses.
medium.q: What are “bells” in the context of the verse?

answers: They will be forbidden for use
They will disappear from the city
Even ordinary vessels will be holy
medium.explanation: Every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be declared holy unto the LORD.
medium.q: What change will occur in the status of ordinary household vessels?

answers: The objects may not be used
challenge.explanation: The passage shows that holiness is no longer limited to formal Temple objects.
challenge.q: What central idea follows from the holiness of both horse bells and pots?

answers: Holy vessels may serve the worship of those who sacrifice
The pots are only for decoration
challenge.explanation: Those who sacrifice will take the pots and seethe their food in them.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the holy pots may be used for cooking?

answers: The world returns to a state of war
Holiness becomes a widespread reality in the city and the Temple
challenge.explanation: The passage presents holiness as encompassing the Temple, the city, and everyday objects.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the idea of a renewed world?
